items.title: Detect actual changed files for active story worktrees
items.context: Collect git-derived changed files for each active story worktree without reading story JSON directly or writing evidence. Include committed branch changes relative to main and uncommitted worktree changes; exclude Lattice runtime/story metadata and non-material runtime artifacts where appropriate.

happy.desc: Two active story worktrees each with committed-vs-main and uncommitted tracked/untracked changes -> parallel_plan/parallel_status/parallel_merge_queue --format=json expose repo-relative POSIX material changed files per story; WHY: core mechanical detection must work without manual sharedHotspots declaration

edge.desc: Active worktree whose only changes are .lattice/** / .koala/** / .omx/** / owner-lease/runtime/cache/log artifacts -> material changed-file set is empty, no overlap reported; WHY: runtime/story-metadata noise must be excluded or every parallel story pair falsely overlaps

adversarial.desc: git probing fails for one story (worktree path missing or git error) -> story kept with a visible degradation marker instead of being silently dropped or throwing; WHY: detection failure must not erase the risk signal or crash the planning surface

verificationEvidence.command: npm --prefix packages/main run build && node packages/main/dist/tasks/lattice-parallel-wave-smoke.js && node packages/main/dist/cli.js parallel_merge_queue --storyIds=["B-8404"] --format=json
verificationEvidence.note: Regression now covers running parallel wave from inside a story worktree; real B-8404 parallel_merge_queue no longer resolves .worktrees/B-8404/.worktrees/B-8404 and still reads changed files from registered worktrees.
Smoke covers metadata-only active worktree changes under .lattice and .koala as ignoredChangedFiles with empty materialChangedFiles and no overlap degradation.

items.title: Integrate changed-file overlap into parallel safety and merge queue guidance
items.context: If two active story worktrees modify the same material file, the wave should surface a visible degradation and avoid recommending simultaneous DEV for those stories. parallel_merge_queue should expose the overlap in blockers/guidance so operators do not merge blindly.

happy.desc: Two active stories modify the same material source file (no sharedHotspots declared) -> both degrade to plan_only in parallel safety output and parallel_merge_queue blockers/guidance include the overlapping file path + peer story id; WHY: this is the core gap the story fixes — overlap must mechanically block simultaneous DEV recommendation

edge.desc: A third non-overlapping active story alongside the overlapping pair -> it remains a parallel_dev candidate when host capability and dependency checks pass, and manually declared sharedHotspots behavior is preserved unchanged; WHY: overlap detection must not over-block clean stories or regress existing hotspot semantics

adversarial.desc: Overlapping story already carries a stronger existing dependency/blocker -> the stronger blocker is preserved (not downgraded or replaced by the overlap degradation) and guidance still surfaces both facts; WHY: precedence under conflicting safety signals must not weaken the stricter constraint

verificationEvidence.note: Smoke asserts overlapping active worktrees degrade to plan_only and merge queue blockers/guidance include the shared file and peer story, including when the projection runs from a story worktree.

items.title: Preserve host-neutral and Authority boundaries
items.context: The new overlap detection must remain L0/read-only planning guidance. It must not mutate story authority, verify receipts, submit evidence, spawn hosts, or claim productionDone/fullAuthorityDone.

happy.desc: Run parallel_plan/parallel_status/parallel_merge_queue with detected overlaps -> JSON output keeps authority.productionDone=false, authority.authorityChanged=false, authority.receiptRefs=[]; WHY: overlap guard is L0 read-only guidance and must never claim Authority completion

edge.desc: Overlap warns/blocks local parallel scheduling -> output text still states it did not prove DONE or Authority completion, and overlap facts are NOT encoded in Authority receipt fields; WHY: blocking guidance must not be misread as authority verdicts

adversarial.desc: Snapshot story metadata/evidence/receipt files before and after running overlap-detection commands -> byte-identical (no story authority mutation, no evidence writes, no receipt verification, no host spawn); WHY: read-only boundary must be proven under operation, not just asserted in docs

verificationEvidence.note: Real CLI projection keeps authority.productionDone=false, authority.authorityChanged=false, receiptRefs=[], and emits only local scheduling guidance after the worktree path fix.

items.title: Add regression coverage for active worktree overlap behavior
items.context: Add smoke coverage proving overlapping active worktree diffs are detected, recommendations are degraded, queue guidance lists the overlap, clean non-overlapping stories remain parallel candidates, and authority fields remain non-authoritative.

happy.desc: npm --prefix packages/main run build && node packages/main/dist/tasks/lattice-parallel-wave-smoke.js -> exit 0 with fixture assertions covering: overlap detected without sharedHotspots, overlapping stories degraded out of parallel_dev, queue guidance lists file + peer story; WHY: deterministic regression proof of the end-to-end overlap behavior

edge.desc: Smoke fixtures where one story changes only Lattice/runtime metadata and another is clean non-overlapping -> no overlap reported for metadata-only diffs and the clean story remains a parallel candidate; WHY: negative coverage prevents false-positive regressions

adversarial.desc: Smoke asserts authority fields stay non-authoritative in overlap scenarios, and assertions are real (a deliberately broken expectation makes the smoke task exit non-zero); WHY: regression coverage that cannot fail is no coverage — the suite must go red when overlap behavior breaks

verificationEvidence.note: Build and smoke pass on the final DEV patch, including regression coverage for relative worktree path resolution from story worktrees and non-authoritative output fields.
